questions.topic_aspect: Reflection in a horizontal or vertical line on a coordinate grid
questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for at least one correct vertex found by correctly reflecting in the horizontal line $y=1$ (i.e. reflecting the $y$-coordinate only, keeping the $x$-coordinate unchanged, using the correct perpendicular distance from $y=1$)
A1 for all three correct image coordinates: $(-4,-1)$, $(-4,-3)$, $(-1,-1)$

Common error (reflecting in $x=1$ or reversing coordinates, e.g. giving $(3,-4)$, $(5,-4)$, $(3,-1)$) scores 0 marks unless method shows correct reflection process for at least one point.
questions.misconception_targeted: Reflecting in the wrong axis or line, or reversing coordinates

questions.topic_aspect: Rotation about the origin by a given angle and direction
questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for correct use of the rotation rule (x, y) → (y, -x) for a 90° clockwise rotation about the origin, applied to at least one vertex (allow if attempted with correct rotation sense even if arithmetic slip on one point)
A1 for at least two correct image coordinates: A' = (1, -1), B' = (1, -3), C' = (3, -3)
A1 for all four correct image coordinates: A' = (1, -1), B' = (1, -3), C' = (3, -3), D' = (2, -1)

Note: award 0 for the M1 if the direction is reversed throughout (i.e. anticlockwise rule (x,y) → (-y, x) used) unless recovered; full marks only for correct clockwise image.
questions.misconception_targeted: Confusing clockwise and anticlockwise direction, or rotating about the wrong centre

questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for adding 3 to each x-coordinate and subtracting 2 from each y-coordinate of at least two vertices (or for one correct translated vertex shown, or attempt to translate all three vertices with correct method but sign/order error).
A1 for all three correct image coordinates: $(-1, 1)$, $(-1, 3)$, $(2, 1)$.
questions.misconception_targeted: Swapping the x and y components of the column vector, or applying the vector with wrong sign

questions.topic_aspect: Enlargement with a positive integer scale factor and given centre (not at origin)
questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for finding the distance (vector) from the centre of enlargement (1,1) to at least one vertex, e.g. A is (1,1) across and up from centre.
M1 for multiplying each of these distances by the scale factor 2 (e.g. new vector from centre to A' is (2,2)) and applying to at least two vertices correctly, or for a fully correct method shown for one vertex.
A1 for all four correct image coordinates: A'(3,3), B'(7,3), C'(7,5), D'(3,5).

Note: Award M0 for candidates who simply add the scale factor (2) to each coordinate, e.g. giving A' = (4,4) instead of (3,3) — this indicates the common misconception of adding the scale factor rather than scaling the distance from the centre of enlargement.
questions.misconception_targeted: Adding scale factor to coordinates instead of scaling distance from centre of enlargement

questions.topic_aspect: Enlargement with a fractional scale factor
questions.mark_scheme:
M1 for multiplying each coordinate of at least three vertices by 1/2 (showing understanding that fractional scale factor reduces the shape, moving points closer to the centre of enlargement)
A1 for at least two correct image coordinates
A1 for all four correct image coordinates: P' = (1, 2), Q' = (3, 2), R' = (3, 1), S' = (1, -1)
(If the student doubles instead of halves the coordinates, e.g. giving P' = (4,8), award 0 marks for that vertex - this indicates the misconception that a fractional scale factor enlarges rather than reduces the shape)
questions.misconception_targeted: Believing a fractional scale factor makes the shape larger, or confusing direction of scaling from centre

questions.topic_aspect: Fully describing a single transformation (rotation) from an object and image, including angle, direction and centre
questions.correct_answer: (a) Rotation. (b) Rotation of $90^\circ$ clockwise about the point $(1,-1)$.
questions.mark_scheme:
(a) B1 for "rotation"
(b) M1 for identifying the angle of rotation as $90^\circ$ (or equivalent, e.g. quarter turn)
A1 for stating the direction as clockwise
A1 for stating the centre of rotation as $(1,-1)$
(Full marks only awarded in (b) if angle, direction AND centre are all correctly stated together; no credit for "rotation" alone as this is already awarded in part (a))
questions.misconception_targeted: Giving an incomplete description (e.g. stating 'rotation' without angle, direction and centre, or 'enlargement' without scale factor and centre)

questions.topic_aspect: Combined transformations in a real-world tracking context (multiple transformations applied in sequence)
questions.mark_scheme:
(a) M1 for adding (2,3) to at least one vertex correctly (e.g. P + (2,3)); A1 for all three correct coordinates: P' = (-3,4), Q' = (-3,6), R' = (-1,4).
(b) M1 for correctly reflecting at least one of the translated vertices in x = 0 (negating the x-coordinate, keeping y-coordinate unchanged), using their (a) values; A1 for all three correct coordinates: P'' = (3,4), Q'' = (3,6), R'' = (1,4). Follow through from part (a) if translation was correct method but arithmetic slip, provided reflection method is correctly applied to their translated points.
questions.misconception_targeted: Applying transformations in the wrong order, or losing track of intermediate coordinates when combining transformations
